question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct for a current carrying solenoid?

(i) It can be used to magnetise a piece of soft iron.

(ii) It acts like a bar magnet

(iii) The field lines are concentric circles
solution:
The correct answer is __**Both (i) and (ii)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A solenoid is a cylindrical coil of wire acting as a magnet when carrying an electric current.
 
• Statement (i) is correct: A current-carrying solenoid produces a magnetic field that can magnetize soft iron, making it useful in electromagnets.
 
• Statement (ii) is correct: A solenoid behaves like a bar magnet with a distinct north and south pole.
 
• Statement (iii) is incorrect: The magnetic field inside a solenoid is uniform and linear, not concentric circles.
 
• The solenoid is widely used in applications such as inductors, electromagnets, and valves due to its ability to generate a strong and uniform magnetic field.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Soft Iron Core:** Soft iron is used in solenoids as it enhances the magnetic field by acting as a temporary magnet when exposed to the solenoid's field.
 
• **Magnetic Field in a Solenoid:** The magnetic field inside a solenoid is nearly uniform and parallel to its axis, whereas the field outside is weaker and non-uniform.
 
• **Field Lines:** Magnetic field lines of a solenoid resemble those of a bar magnet, with lines entering at one end (south pole) and exiting at the other end (north pole).
 
• **Applications of Solenoids:** Solenoids are commonly used in devices like relays, valves, MRI machines, and electromagnetic locks.
 
• **Electromagnetism:** A solenoid demonstrates the principles of electromagnetism, where electric current generates a magnetic field. This principle is crucial in various industrial and scientific applications.
